messages:
tess: heads up — customer tenant-acme-42 reporting repeated 429s + higher token latency on their Dedicated pool since ~09:30 UTC. They said this started after yesterday's quota migration. link to convo: https://redwood/support/12345 :sos:
liam: can you paste the tenant id + a sample failed request/response headers?

tess: tenant: tenant-acme-42
response: 429 Too Many Requests
headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-Redwood-Rate-Limit: 0/60
```

kelsey: CS got an angry PM. They saw their billed units drop ~10x after migration. asked for escalation.

ashwin: quick theory — our rate-limiter mapping may have interpreted legacy quotas (units/min) as units/sec after the migration. that would massively tighten caps. also saw autoscaler metric name changed in the same deploy so scaling didn't react.

marc: on it — looking at /etc/redwood/rate-mapping.yaml for that tenant now.

marc: found entry: `tenant-acme-42: 6000` — comments say "legacy: units/min" but our runtime now treats numbers as units/s. so 6000/min -> 6000/s effective cap which is actually higher, hmm. need to check conversion path used during migration.

ashwin: if the migration converted wrong direction (interpreting min as sec or vice versa) you can end up 60x mismatch either way. request logs show X-Redwood-Rate-Limit: 0/60 which implies we limited them to 60 rps equivalent. looks like new schema expected per-minute but we wrote per-second.

liam: can you run a quick local repro? simplest: run hey or a short ab load against a dedicated endpoint with tenant header to see 429 pattern. e.g.
```
hey -n 500 -c 50 -H "x-tenant-id: tenant-acme-42" https://dedicated-us.redwood/v1/generate
```

ashwin: i'm also checking autoscaler logs — autoscaler ignored the pool because metric filter expects `redwood.runtime.queue_depth.v2` but deploy wrote `queue_depth`. autoscale rule returned empty so no scale up. will re-enable the backward compatible metric name for now.

marc: quick mitigation applied: converted tenant-acme-42 quota to explicit rps override and enabled burst capacity on that dedicated pool. command used: `rctl override set --tenant tenant-acme-42 --rps 60 --burst 120`

deploy-bot: rollout started for patch `199876-rl-migration-fix` across dedicated-rate-limiter (1/3 nodes updated).

liam: also pushed hotfix to autoscaler config: accept both `queue_depth` and `queue_depth.v2` tags. will watch metrics for next 15m.

kelsey: told customer we applied temporary override and are rolling a fix. PM said immediate 429s stopped but they see occasional latency spikes.

ashwin: follow-up actions:
- audit migration scripts for unit conversion bugs
- add validation to reject ambiguous unit fields (require explicit ":/s" or "/m")
- add smoke test that simulates high-concurrency tenant load after migration
- add telemetry alert if per-tenant consumption suddenly changes > 10x post-migration

marc: agreed. i also put a note in the Dedicated runbook to check autoscaler metric names after deploys.

tess: customer confirmed 429 rate down to near zero after our override. asked for ETA on permanent fix. i'll post updates. :thumbsup:

kelsey: flagged for priority follow-up tomorrow 09:00 PT.

liam: monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/prod/dedicated/tenant-acme-42 — CPU + queue_depth trending back to normal.

marc: closing temporary escalation ticket after post-deploy verification. will open follow-up for migration audit. :white_check_mark:
